MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Lead the operations that enable exceptional care.

At Anglicare Sydney, we believe great services begin with great operations. Behind every welcoming reception, safe workplace and well-supported team is a leader who keeps everything running smoothly.

For over 170 years, Anglicare has been serving people in need, enriching lives and strengthening communities through compassionate, values-driven care.

Our vision is simple yet powerful:

Jesus Christ honoured, lives enriched and communities strengthened.

About the role

As Site Operations Manager, you'll lead the operational functions that keep our sites running effectively. Working closely with Program Managers, Heads of Practice and corporate support teams, you'll oversee administration, workplace operations, WHS, facilities coordination and site-based projects while leading a team of Administration Coordinators and Receptionists.

You'll be a key driver of continuous improvement, ensuring our sites operate efficiently, comply with organisational standards and provide an outstanding experience for clients, staff and visitors.

In this role you'll

Lead the day-to-day operations across Community & Mission sites, ensuring safe, efficient and welcoming environments.

Provide leadership, coaching and support to Administration Coordinators, Receptionists and site administration teams.

Manage workplace operations including reception services, facilities, contractor coordination, repairs and maintenance.

Oversee site administration, financial processing and operational systems that support service delivery.

Coordinate Work Health and Safety activities, emergency management, site inspections and compliance initiatives.

Partner with Property, IT, Finance, Payroll, Marketing, Learning & Development and other corporate teams to optimise site operations.

Lead operational projects and implement initiatives that improve service delivery and staff experience.

Coordinate site meetings, events, inductions and cross-functional collaboration.

Develop and maintain operational procedures, ensuring consistency across multiple sites.

Build strong relationships with internal stakeholders, community partners and church representatives.

Monitor operational performance and identify opportunities for continuous improvement.

About you

You're an experienced operations leader who enjoys creating systems that enable people to do their best work.

You thrive in a fast-paced environment, can confidently manage competing priorities and enjoy building collaborative relationships across diverse teams.

Demonstrated experience in operations, business administration or office management within a complex organisation.

Proven leadership experience managing administration or operational teams.

Strong stakeholder management and relationship-building skills.

Experience managing facilities, contractors and workplace operations.

Knowledge of Work Health and Safety legislation and operational compliance.

Strong financial administration and budget management skills.

Experience leading projects and driving continuous improvement initiatives.

Excellent organisational, communication and problem-solving skills.

Ability to manage multiple sites and priorities simultaneously.

Intermediate to advanced Microsoft Office skills and confidence learning new systems.

A commitment to Anglicare's Christian values and person-centred approach.

Essential requirements

Relevant tertiary qualifications in Business, Management or a related discipline (or equivalent experience).

Current NSW Driver Licence.

National Police Check (or willingness to obtain).

Working With Children Check.

NDIS Worker Check.

Demonstrated leadership experience in an operational environment.

Why Anglicare?

At Anglicare, you'll join one of Australia's largest and most respected Christian care organisations, where your leadership will directly support the delivery of life-changing services.

Salary packaging to maximise your take-home pay.

Ongoing leadership development and career progression opportunities.

A supportive and collaborative leadership team.

Opportunities to lead meaningful operational improvements across multiple sites.

A values-driven culture where your work contributes to stronger communities every day.

Ready to make an impact?

If you're a proactive operational leader who enjoys improving systems, leading teams and creating exceptional workplace experiences, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply now by submitting your resume and cover letter.

Boilermaker – Full-Time

Location: Welshpool, Western Australia 6106
Employment Type: Full-Time
Salary: $80,000 – $110,000 per annum (depending on skills and experience)

MINPROVISE INTERNATIONAL PTY LTD is a leading total solutions provider delivering specialist maintenance and shutdown services, engineering, fabrication, project services, and sustaining capital works. We also provide a comprehensive range of equipment and products, supporting the mining, oil & gas, and construction industries across Australia and internationally.

We are currently seeking experienced and motivated Boilermakers to join our growing team on a full-time basis.
About the Role

As a Boilermaker, you will be responsible for fabricating, assembling, installing, maintaining, and repairing structural steel, pressure vessels, heavy equipment, and metal components used in mining, industrial, and construction projects. You will work closely with engineers, supervisors, and maintenance teams to ensure all fabrication and welding work is completed safely, efficiently, and in accordance with engineering specifications and Australian Standards.

Key Responsibilities
•	Read and interpret engineering drawings, blueprints, fabrication plans, and technical specifications.
•	Fabricate, assemble, install, and repair structural steel, heavy machinery components, tanks, chutes, hoppers, conveyors, and other metal 
structures.

Bowhill Engineering is entering an exciting new stage of growth, and we're looking for an experienced and people-focused Business Manager to help lead the business through its next chapter.
This is a unique opportunity to play a pivotal leadership role within a growing engineering and manufacturing business, helping strengthen our systems, support our people, and build the structure required to successfully grow from approximately 60 employees to 90+ and beyond.
Specialising in major infrastructure projects and complexity done excellently, Bowhill Engineering is powered by technology and driven by great people to optimise and build structures that matter.


About the Role
The Business Manager will provide leadership, coordination and accountability across our key business support functions, including Human Resources, Administration, WHSE and Finance.
Working closely with the CEO, senior leaders and support teams, you will become the central point of coordination that helps ensure communication is clear, priorities are aligned, systems continue to improve, and important initiatives are delivered successfully.
This role is not about doing everything yourself. It is about leading people, strengthening accountability, improving processes, supporting teams and ensuring the business operates efficiently while maintaining the practical, down-to-earth culture that makes Bowhill Engineering a great place to work.
You will help create the systems, structure and leadership pathways needed to support sustainable growth while preserving the values and culture that have made Bowhill Engineering successful.


Key Responsibilities
-Provide leadership and coordination across HR, Administration, WHSE and Finance support functions
-Act as the central point of contact for internal business support activities
-Support the CEO and Leadership Team by reducing day-to-day operational distractions
-Improve communication, clarity and accountability across teams
-Drive implementation of new systems, processes and business improvement initiatives
-Monitor business performance and ensure key priorities are followed through
-Build capability within support teams through coaching, guidance and leadership
-Strengthen succession planning and reduce key-person dependencies
-Support business growth by developing scalable systems and structures
-Foster a positive workplace culture aligned with Bowhill Engineering's values

About You
You enjoy bringing order to complexity and helping people succeed.
You are practical, organised and commercially minded, with the ability to balance strategic thinking with hands-on leadership. You communicate clearly, follow through on commitments and know how to achieve results through collaboration and accountability.
You may come from a business management, operations, HR, finance, administration or leadership background. Most importantly, you understand how businesses operate and can bring people, systems and priorities together to achieve positive outcomes.
You will be:
-Highly organised, practical and reliable
-A strong communicator with excellent interpersonal skills
-Commercially aware with sound financial understanding
-Confident leading people and managing accountability
-Calm under pressure and able to prioritise effectively
-Comfortable working with both senior leaders and frontline teams
-Respectful, humble and solutions-focused
-A proactive problem solver who takes ownership and follows through
-Adaptable and quick to learn new systems and processes

Skills & Experience
-Qualification in Business, Management, Human Resources, Finance, Marketing or a related discipline (desirable)
-Demonstrated experience in a senior business, operations, administration, HR, finance or management role
-Strong business acumen with experience managing budgets, reporting and business performance
-Proven leadership experience with the ability to coordinate teams and drive accountability
-Experience implementing and improving systems, processes and business initiatives
-Excellent organisational, communication and problem-solving skills
-Strong computer literacy including Microsoft Office and business management systems
-Ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced and growing environment

What We Offer
-A key leadership role within a growing and ambitious organisation
-Opportunity to help shape the future direction of the business
-Direct collaboration with the CEO and Leadership Team
-Long-term career growth and development opportunities
-Annual wage reviews and professional development support
-Employee Assistance Program (EAP)Employee Health Assistance
-Active Social Club and strong team culture
-Modern workplace and supportive environment
-Enjoy the River Murray lifestyle
-Join an Employer of Choice in the Murraylands

Why Bowhill Engineering?
At Bowhill Engineering, culture matters.
We value honesty, humility, teamwork, respect and doing what we say we're going to do. We are proud of the projects we deliver, the people we employ and the communities we support.
This is an opportunity to step into a meaningful leadership role and help shape the next chapter of Bowhill Engineering while ensuring we continue to grow without losing what makes us unique.


How to Apply
Applications must be submitted via our website

Rigger – Full-Time
Location: Welshpool, Western Australia 6106
Employment Type: Full-Time
Salary: $80,000 – $110,000 per annum (depending on skills and experience)

MINPROVISE INTERNATIONAL PTY LTD is a leading total solutions provider delivering specialist maintenance and shutdown services, engineering, fabrication, project services, and sustaining capital works. We also provide a comprehensive range of equipment and products, supporting the mining, oil & gas, and construction industries across Australia and internationally.

We are currently seeking experienced and motivated Riggers to join our growing team on a full-time basis.

About the Role
As a Rigger, you will be responsible for planning, preparing, and performing rigging operations to safely lift, move, position, and secure heavy machinery, structural steel, equipment, and materials across mining, oil & gas, construction, and industrial projects. You will work closely with crane operators, engineers, supervisors, and other trades to ensure lifting activities are carried out safely and efficiently in accordance with Australian Standards and site requirements.

Key Responsibilities
•	Read and interpret lifting plans, engineering drawings, and work instructions.
•	Plan and perform rigging operations for lifting, positioning, and installation of heavy equipment and structural components.
•	Select, inspect, and safely use lifting gear, including slings, chains, wire ropes, shackles, spreader bars, lifting beams, and hoists.
•	Direct crane operators using standard hand signals and radio communications during lifting operations.
•	Assemble, dismantle, align, and secure heavy machinery, plant, structural steel, and industrial equipment.
•	Conduct pre-start inspections of rigging equipment and ensure all lifting gear is certified and fit for use.
•	Identify hazards, assess lifting risks, and implement appropriate control measures.
•	Assist with shutdowns, maintenance projects, equipment installations, and major construction activities.
•	Maintain accurate records of lifting equipment inspections and completed work where required.
•	Work collaboratively with supervisors, engineers, crane operators, and other trades to ensure projects are completed safely and on schedule.
•	Follow all workplace health and safety policies, procedures, and environmental requirements.

Skills and Experience
•	Minimum 1–2 years of full-time experience as a Rigger in mining, construction, or heavy industrial environments.
•	Current High Risk Work Licence – Rigging (Basic, Intermediate, or Advanced).
•	Strong knowledge of lifting techniques, rigging equipment, and safe lifting practices.
•	Ability to read and interpret lifting plans, engineering drawings, and technical specifications.
•	Experience working with cranes, heavy equipment, structural steel, and mechanical installations.
•	Strong commitment to workplace safety and compliance with Australian Standards.
•	Ability to work independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team.
•	Excellent communication, problem-solving, and organisational skills.

What We Offer
•	Full-time, permanent employment.
•	Competitive salary of $80,000 – $110,000 per annum.
•	Opportunities to work on major mining, shutdown, and industrial projects.
•	Ongoing training and career development.
•	Supportive team environment with long-term career opportunities.
